review_evidence: Codex self-review: pedagogy, answer keys, concept slots, unseen passages, age fit, and source independence
title: Best Friends
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Why friends work better together
levels.teaching_goal: Understand that different friends can each add something useful, then explain the lesson in a short answer.

guided_check.teaching_block: In this chapter, shape friends first compare themselves. A strong answer should move from 'who is best' to 'what can they do as a team'.
guided_check.passage: Circle can make a sun. Triangle can make a roof. Square can make a window. Rectangle can make a door.
guided_check.prompt: What should the shape friends do to make one complete picture?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: each shape is useful in a different way. When useful parts join, the picture becomes better.
bridge.passage: One shape makes the sun. Another shape makes the roof. Another makes the door.
bridge.prompt: Which idea helps all shapes make a better picture?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: the main idea is the lesson that covers the whole story. Here the lesson is not that one shape wins. The lesson is that friends can create more together.
masterclass.passage: Four children each know one part of a song. When they sing together, the song is complete.

independent_check.teaching_block: Now answer without hints. Write the lesson in your own words.
independent_check.passage: The shape friends stop arguing and make a picture by using each shape well.
independent_check.prompt: What lesson do the shape friends learn?

concept_slots.description: refers to the shapes or friends as a group
states that different parts become useful when they work together

transfer_check.teaching_block: Carry the teamwork lesson into a task without shapes.
transfer_check.passage: For a class play, Ina remembers the lines, Faraz makes props, and Diya plays music. The show needs all three jobs.
transfer_check.prompt: Explain why the children should work as a team.

concept_slots.description: recognises that the children contribute different jobs or strengths
explains that combining the jobs helps complete the play

levels.title: Use shape clues
levels.focus: use context to understand a word
levels.teaching_goal: Use clues like round, sides, corners, and roof to identify shape words.

guided_check.teaching_block: A clue can tell us the shape even when we are not shown a picture. Round and no corners point to a circle.
guided_check.passage: Nina draws a round moon. It has no corners.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: count sides and corners. Three sides often point to a triangle.
bridge.passage: The kite has three sharp corners and three sides.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: match the clue to the shape feature. Equal sides can point to a square; two long sides and two short sides can point to a rectangle.
masterclass.passage: A small tile has four equal sides.
masterclass.prompt: Which shape clue fits the tile?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now use the clue without help.
independent_check.passage: The roof in the drawing has three sides and sits above the house.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use shape clues in an object outside a drawing lesson.
transfer_check.passage: A warning sign has three straight sides and three corners.
transfer_check.prompt: Write the shape of the sign.

levels.title: Use a and an
levels.teaching_goal: Choose a before consonant sounds and an before vowel sounds in simple sentences.

guided_check.teaching_block: Use 'an' before words that begin with a vowel sound. The word umbrella begins with a vowel sound.
guided_check.passage: Meera carries ___ umbrella on a rainy day.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: say the first sound. Apple starts with a vowel sound, so we say an apple.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: do not look for any vowel anywhere in the word. Listen to the first sound: a star begins with a consonant sound; an orange begins with a vowel sound.
masterclass.passage: Tara draws ___ star and ___ orange sun.

independent_check.passage: Ayan draws ___ square on his notebook.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use the starting-sound rule with a new pair of objects.
transfer_check.passage: Neha packed ___ orange and ___ banana for the trip.
transfer_check.prompt: Write the two articles in order.

levels.title: Write about a friend
levels.teaching_goal: Write a simple complete sentence that tells one clear quality of a friend.

guided_check.teaching_block: A complete sentence can tell one thing about a friend. Use a describing word like kind, helpful, funny, or brave.
guided_check.passage: My friend helps me carry my books.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: first choose the quality, then put it in a sentence.
bridge.passage: Reva shares her crayons with others.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: one describing word such as helpful is only a fragment. A complete friend sentence needs a naming part and a telling part: 'My friend is helpful.'
masterclass.passage: Kabir waits for his friend and helps him finish the drawing.

independent_check.teaching_block: Now write one complete sentence about a friend.
independent_check.passage: Think of a friend who helps others.
independent_check.prompt: Write one complete sentence about that friend.

concept_slots.description: names or clearly refers to a friend
states a helpful friendship quality or action

transfer_check.teaching_block: Describe a teammate in a new setting with a complete idea.
transfer_check.passage: During a relay game, one teammate waits calmly and cheers when others run.
transfer_check.prompt: Write one complete sentence describing this teammate.

concept_slots.description: describes patience, support, or encouragement shown in the scene

levels.title: Find action words
levels.teaching_goal: Identify action words that tell what a person, animal, or thing does.

guided_check.teaching_block: An action word tells what someone or something does. In 'Dogs bark at the gate', bark is the action.
guided_check.passage: Dogs bark when they hear a knock.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: ask, 'What do they do?' Birds sing, children run, monkeys jump.
bridge.passage: Monkeys jump from branch to branch.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: do not choose cats or birds just because they come first. Those words name; sleep and fly tell what they do.
masterclass.passage: Cats sleep in the shade. Birds fly above the tree.
masterclass.prompt: Which pair has two action words?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now find the action word without hints.
independent_check.passage: The children jump near the painted shapes.
independent_check.prompt: Which verb names what the baker does?

transfer_check.teaching_block: Find an action word in a setting away from the shape picture.
transfer_check.passage: The baker kneads soft dough before sunrise.
